about: The nine Planetary Boundaries and their control variables, as Table 7.1 of the Planetary Health Check 2026 gives them (current, reference, boundary and high-risk values), beside the assessment it compares itself with, Richardson et al. (2023). Each boundary's status in words is the report's own.

boundaries.name: Climate change
boundaries.summary: Atmospheric CO₂ and the radiative forcing humans add both exceed their boundaries: rising temperatures, extreme weather, sea-level rise.

boundaries.name: Biosphere integrity
boundaries.summary: Species are going extinct far faster than the background rate, and humans take a large share of the energy plants capture: both in the high-risk zone.

variables.name: Extinctions
variables.note: Extinctions per million species-years. A range in 2026 (100–1000), and “more than 100” in 2023: the report blurs its wedge's end.

variables.name: Energy taken from ecosystems
variables.note: Human appropriation of net primary production, as a share of the pre-industrial. Several estimates in 2026, 21–30%.

boundaries.name: Land system change
boundaries.summary: Forest cover across the forest biomes has fallen below the safe level, through farming, logging and, increasingly, heat, drought and fire.

variables.name: Forest cover
variables.note: 64% in 2026 against 60% in 2023, and a boundary of 78% against 75%: a corrected method and more complete data, the report says, not forest recovering.

boundaries.name: Freshwater change
boundaries.summary: Humans have disturbed both the water in rivers (blue) and the water in soils (green) beyond safe levels.

variables.name: Blue water
variables.note: The share of land where river flow departs from its pre-industrial range.

variables.name: Green water
variables.note: The share of land where soil moisture departs from its pre-industrial range.

boundaries.name: Nitrogen and phosphorus
boundaries.summary: Fertiliser has pushed nitrogen and phosphorus flows far beyond safe levels: polluted water, algal blooms, dead zones.

variables.name: Phosphorus to the ocean
variables.note: The 2026 table gives 4.4 Tg/yr, inside the boundary of 11, where 2023 gave 22.6; the report's text still calls both nutrient boundaries strongly transgressed, and lists no new data for them. Shown as the table gives it.

boundaries.name: Ocean acidification
boundaries.summary: Assessed as transgressed for the first time: the ocean takes up our CO₂ and turns harder on shells and skeletons, most of all in the Arctic and Southern Oceans.

variables.name: Aragonite saturation
variables.note: Just past its boundary in 2026 (2.85 against 2.86), with four data products where 2023 had one.

boundaries.name: Aerosol loading
boundaries.summary: Within the boundary globally, and improving; but over South Asia, above a proposed regional boundary that may disturb the monsoon.

variables.name: Aerosols over South Asia
variables.note: A proposed regional boundary, new in 2026, with no reference value given: drawn from zero. It does not count towards the global status.

boundaries.name: Stratospheric ozone
boundaries.summary: Back within the boundary, thanks to the controls on CFCs, though below mid-20th-century levels and perhaps recovering more slowly.

boundaries.name: Novel entities
boundaries.summary: Synthetic chemicals, plastics and PFASs are released faster than they can be tested; the report places this in the high-risk zone, though no zone has a number yet.

variables.name: Chemicals released untested
variables.note: The boundary is zero: none released without adequate safety testing. The zones beyond it have no numbers; the report places the current state in the high-risk zone, its wedge's end blurred.
